message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of solid, beginner‑friendly leg exercises you can add to your routine. I’ll give you a mix of compound moves (that hit multiple muscles at once) and isolation moves (targeting specific areas). Feel free to pick a few that fit your goals and equipment availability.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles Worked | Key Tips |
|----------|------------------------|----------|
| **Squat** (bodyweight or barbell) | Quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings, core | Keep your chest up, knees tracking over toes, sit back into hips. |
| **Lunge** (forward, reverse, walking) | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Step far enough that the front knee stays above the ankle; keep torso upright. |
| **Deadlift** (conventional or sumo) | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back, traps | Maintain a neutral spine, pull through heels, keep the bar close to your shins. |
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Adjust foot placement to target different parts of the quads; avoid locking out knees. |
| **Calf Raise** (standing or seated) | Gastrocnemius, soleus | Full range of motion—rise onto toes, then lower all the way down. |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Place rear foot on bench; keep front knee aligned with ankle. |
| **Step‑Up** (onto bench or box) | Quads, glutes, calves | Drive through the heel of the stepping foot; keep the movement controlled. |
| **Hamstring Curl** (lying or seated machine) | Hamstrings | Focus on squeezing at the top; avoid using momentum. |
| **Glute Bridge / Hip Thrust** | Glutes, hamstrings, lower back | Squeeze glutes at the top; keep hips in line with shoulders. |
| **Bodyweight Wall Sit** | Quads, glutes | Hold the position for time; keep knees at a 90° angle. |

### How to Structure a Leg Workout

1. **Warm‑up** – 5–10 min light cardio (bike, jog) + dynamic stretches (leg swings, hip circles).
2. **Compound lifts first** – Start with squats or deadlifts when you’re fresh.
3. **Add isolation work** – After the heavy lifts, move to calf raises, hamstring curls, or glute bridges.
4. **Cool‑down** – Light stretching focusing on quads, hamstrings, calves, and hips.

### Sample Beginner Routine (3× per week)

| Day | Sets × Reps | Exercise |
|-----|-------------|----------|
| **Day 1** | 3×8 | Back Squat |
| | 3×10 | Walking Lunge |
| | 3×12 | Seated Calf Raise |
| | 3×15 | Bodyweight Wall Sit |
| **Day 2** | 3×8 | Romanian Deadlift |
| | 3×10 | Bulgarian Split Squat |
| | 3×12 | Lying Hamstring Curl |
| | 3×15 | Glute Bridge |
| **Day 3** | 3×8 | Front Squat |
| | 3×10 | Step‑Up |
| | 3×12 | Standing Calf Raise |
| | 3×15 | Bodyweight Wall Sit |

Feel free to swap in variations (sumo deadlift, goblet squat, single‑leg calf raise) as you progress. If you have access to a gym, adding weighted versions will help build strength faster. If you’re working out at home, bodyweight or resistance bands can still give you a great workout. Happy training!
